newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel calls again for German cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Waigel calls again for German cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Thursday shrugged off a rebuff by Chancellor Helmut Kohl and repeated his call for a cabinet reshuffle soon.
Waigel told Bild newspaper a shakeup would make Kohl's 17-member cabinet more effective in the runup to the September 1998 general election.
"The chancellor has the right a year before the elections to put together a team with which he would want to rule for four years," Waigel said. "I would expect the coalition to gain extra momentum."
Waigel, post-war Germany's longest-serving finance minister, has had his reputation dented by numerous setbacks in his efforts to qualify for Europe's single currency and pass key tax reforms.

When the going has got tough in the past, speculation has mounted that he might take over the foreign affairs portfolio, handing the job of finance minister to the Free Democrats in the coalition, who are explicitly committed to tax cuts.
But Waigel told Bild he was not seeking to grab Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel's job.
"Honestly. I wasn't thinking about myself at all. I enjoy my job," Waigel said.
"I'm talking about something else. It is already clear that one or two ministers...in the government want to quit after the next general election.
"It is legitimate to say: Let's bring forward these changes -- which would be necessary anyway after the elections -- to help the coalition."
Waigel said it would also make sense to consider a further reduction in the number of ministerial positions after the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry is abolished this autumn.
Kohl, on holiday in Austria, made clear through a government spokesman earlier this week that he had no intention of rejigging his government -- at least for now.
